value: Privileged accounts create critical security exposure and may be exploited by insider or external threats.
Excessive, standing, or unauthorized privileged access may violate least-privilege and need-to-know principles.
Unvaulted, shared, or inadequately rotated credentials may be compromised or misused.
Unrecorded or insufficiently monitored privileged sessions may hinder detection and investigation of misuse.
Uncertified, orphaned, or outdated access may remain active after review deadlines or workforce changes.
Vendor or third-party privileged access may create security exposure if it is not restricted, monitored, or time-limited.
Break-glass access may be misused or inadequately documented.
Grant privileged access according to least-privilege and need-to-know principles, using approval workflows based on system classification.
Prohibit permanent or standing privileged access for human users; require temporary, auto-expiring access.
Store, rotate, and check out administrative credentials through the enterprise PAM vault; prohibit direct login without vault mediation.
Require separate standard and privileged accounts, with the privileged account using the priv_ prefix.
Vault built-in root and administrator accounts and rotate their passwords after every use or every 24 hours.
Ban shared logins unless technically impossible; require session recording when they are used.
Require phishing-resistant FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware-key MFA for all privileged logins.
Automatically terminate privileged sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Record production, payment gateway, and core database sessions in real time, including video and commands.
Capture user ID, vaulted session ID, source IP address, commands, target system, and precise UTC timestamps in system logs.
Stream privileged activity audit logs to a WORM central SIEM and retain them for at least 24 months, or 7 years for financial and tax systems.
Use real-time behavioral analytics to alert the SOC to out-of-hours access, concurrent multi-location logins, and unauthorized privilege escalation commands.
Review and recertify Tier 1 production and critical-system access monthly by System Owners; review Tier 2 general enterprise access quarterly.
Automatically revoke uncertified access within 48 hours after a passed review deadline and retain review sign-off evidence at IAG.

Revoke privileged credentials, sessions, and access within 1 hour of HR notification of involuntary termination; revoke voluntary-resignation access at the end of the final working day; revoke access tied to a previous role within 24 hours of an effective transfer.
Authorize vendor access through a Senior Director, restrict it to dedicated Jump Hosts, and require session recording.
Limit vendor access to no more than 8 consecutive hours per session request; prohibit permanent external access.
Require real-time monitoring or post-session review of vendor activity by a designated internal System Owner.
Restrict break-glass credentials to active outages or P1 incidents, seal them in the PAM vault, and require dual-custody authorization by two designated security leaders.
Require full audit logging and justification of break-glass use to be submitted to the CISO and IAG within 24 hours of incident closure.
Require temporary exceptions to have a documented risk assessment, compensating security controls, and formal CISO and Enterprise Risk Committee sign-off; limit exceptions to 90 days.
Treat bypassing PAM controls, credential sharing, or disabling session logging as a critical security breach subject to immediate access revocation and escalation.
